raw_response:
I'm 53 years old and I've been farming these fields in Quzhou County since I was a teenager helping my father. I never went to school, but I know this land and I know what works here. Every year I plant winter wheat after the National Day holiday in October, and then right after harvesting the wheat in early June, I put in summer maize. That's what everyone in my village does, and that's what the land is good for.

This year I'll plant 8 mu of wheat and 8 mu of maize on the same flat irrigated land. I buy improved wheat seeds from the agricultural supply store in town — the shopkeeper recommends varieties like Jimai 22, and I trust him because he knows what grows well around here. For maize, I always buy hybrid seeds, usually Denghai 605. My own saved seeds don't grow well for maize, and everyone knows that.

For fertilizer, I spread compound fertilizer when I prepare the land for wheat, then top-dress with urea when the wheat greens up in spring and again at jointing. The maize gets some fertilizer at planting and one more top-dressing when it's about knee-high. I don't count exact kilograms in my head — I buy bags and spread them the way I've always done, about the same as my neighbors do.

I irrigate the wheat three times: once to help it through winter, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. The maize usually needs two irrigations in summer if the rain doesn't come. I till the wheat field with the rotary tiller to break up the soil, but for maize I sow directly into the wheat stubble without tilling — that saves time and fuel, and the shopkeeper says it's fine now.

I spray pesticides a few times each season when I see insects or when the shop tells me others are spraying. I expect about 500 kg per mu of wheat and around 550 kg per mu of maize if the weather is normal. I don't grow cotton or vegetables because I don't have the extra labor or the know-how, and wheat and maize have buyers who come right to the village. The government guarantees a price for wheat, so I know I won't lose money on that. That's my security.
